parts.label: a
parts.reason: Spearman's rank correlation is not mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements; only PMCC (calculator) is mentioned and even that is excluded from formula calculation. Spearman's rank is a distinct named concept not covered.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for Spearman's rank correlation
parts.reason: Depends on part (a)'s Spearman's rank value and is a significance test for rank correlation, not mentioned in S5.1 (which only covers PMCC, with derivation excluded). Out of spec.

parts.label: main
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests, contingency tables, and degrees of freedom for independence testing are not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement. S2.4 explicitly limits significance tests to those in Section 5, which only covers binomial proportion and Normal mean tests.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Confidence intervals are not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement (S5.3 covers hypothesis testing for the mean, not CIs). Named concept absent from spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Binomial probability applied to confidence intervals
parts.reason: Although the binomial calculation itself is S4.1-type, this uses the concept of a confidence interval containing μ (from out-of-spec part (a)), a concept not in spec; the part only makes sense after the out-of-spec confidence interval concept.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly lists stratified sampling as a technique students should be familiar with.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for difference of two means (Normal approximation, two independent samples)
parts.reason: S5.3 only covers a test for the mean of a single Normal distribution; a two-sample test for difference of means is not mentioned anywhere in the statements.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: S5.3 explicitly excludes knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem.

parts.label: d
parts.reason: Relates to the out-of-spec two-sample hypothesis test; not covered by any statement.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Interpretation of two-sample hypothesis test result
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec two-sample test in (b).

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Comment on effectiveness based on test outcomes
parts.reason: Depends entirely on out-of-spec parts (b) and (e).

parts.label: a
parts.reason: S4.1 covers using the binomial distribution as a model and commenting critically on appropriateness, which includes assumptions.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Mean from frequency table (grouped data mean)
parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of central tendency including mean calculation from data.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: S4.1 covers calculating probabilities using the binomial distribution; computing expected frequencies from binomial probabilities is a direct application.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test for binomial distribution
parts.reason: Chi-squared goodness of fit tests are not mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements; S2.4 restricts significance tests to those in Section 5 (binomial proportion, Normal mean), which does not include goodness-of-fit testing.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Linear combination of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: S4.2 covers the Normal distribution as a model and finding probabilities, but forming and using the distribution of a linear combination (B - 1.1R) of two independent Normal variables is not mentioned in any statement; this is a distinct technique beyond simple probability lookup.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Distribution of difference of two independent identical Normal random variables
parts.reason: Same issue as (a): combining Normal random variables via sums/differences is not covered by S4.2, which only addresses finding probabilities for a single Normal distribution.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Distribution of sums of multiple independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: Requires combining sums of 10/11 independent Normal variables plus another Normal variable, a technique not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement.
